text:
PART B SCOPED PROPERLY, AND MY HANDOFF OVERSTATED HOW FREE IT IS. Measured at 19:50, no build required.

I wrote in the end-of-day handoff that Part B "needs no corpus, no provider, no owner decision". The first two are true. What I did not check before saying it is WHETHER A SECOND FIXTURE EXISTS TO POINT THE CLI AT. It does not.

  StoryModel[ModelStatus.Validated] appears in 13 files. Exactly ONE is a hand-authored story:
  WarOfTheGhostsModel.scala, 1526 LINES. BirthdayInterview is an InterviewModel -- a different type,
  not a second story.

So "point the CLI at a second fixture" cannot be done by wiring up something that already exists. Authoring a second real story model by hand is days of work, not the small slice I described.

BUT THERE ARE TWO CHEAPER ROUTES AND THE BEAD'S ACTUAL GOAL SURVIVES. The goal was never "have two stories" -- it was to prove Edition.build's generality is A FACT RATHER THAN A SIGNATURE, since it takes StoryModel[Validated] and has only ever been called with one value.

  ROUTE 1, SMALLEST: codec/src/test/.../CodecGens.scala:574 already has
    lazy val validated: StoryModel[ModelStatus.Validated]
  a synthetic validated model. It is in TEST scope, so a CLI cannot reach it. Promoting a small
  synthetic generator into main scope, or adding an equivalent under fixtures, gives Edition.build a
  SECOND VALUE to render. That proves generality mechanically. It does NOT prove the renderer
  produces anything a human would want to look at, and whoever does it should say so rather than
  claiming more.

  ROUTE 2, REAL BUT GATED: document/compiler.scala:595 exposes
    def validated: Option[StoryModel[ModelStatus.Validated]]
  so the NarrativeCompiler already produces validated models. That is the honest path to a second
  STORY rather than a second VALUE -- and it needs compilation input, which is Stage 1b, which is
  the blocker Part A already has.

RECOMMENDATION: Route 1, explicitly labelled as what it is. Rendering a synthetic model answers "can Edition.build render anything but WOG" with a yes or a no, today, for a few hours' work. If it says NO -- if the renderer has quietly grown WOG-shaped assumptions -- that is a finding worth having before anyone builds the input path on top of it. If it says yes, the CLI work ahead really is small, which is what the bead currently ASSERTS and nobody has checked.

WHY I AM CORRECTING MYSELF HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY: I listed this first in the handoff as the thing needing nothing from anybody, which would have sent the next actor at a task whose first hour is discovering there is no second fixture. That is the same defect I have been naming all day -- a claim about the world that nobody measured, made by me, in a document meant to orient someone else.
